disease_label_per_paper: Relapse of typhoid fever following delayed response to meropenem
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 18-year-old man presented with watery diarrhea, high-grade fever, and severe malaise after returning from multi-country travel including Nepal and India.
Five days after returning from travel he developed fever, chills, cough, sore throat, and headache; diarrhea began after 3 days, and total illness duration at admission was 7 days.
Examination showed exsiccosis, relative bradycardia with pulse 95/min despite temperature 39 degC, hypotension 95/60 mmHg, normal ECG, and otherwise unremarkable exam.
Initial labs showed discrete thrombocytopenia, elevated CRP, mild transaminitis, and elevated LDH; malaria thick smear and rapid test were negative.

Blood cultures later grew gram-negative bacteria and then Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. He received ceftriaxone, was switched to meropenem, recovered, then relapsed 14 days after treatment completion with recurrent fever, crampy abdominal pain, and watery diarrhea.

quality_warnings: Salmonella Typhi culture/speciation and susceptibility are stored in confirmatory_findings or microbiology, not as ordinary diagnostic observations.
The article reports CRP as 93 mg/dl with normal <5; this case stores 93 mg/L because the stated reference range matches mg/L reporting.
Initial WBC count is described as normal but no numeric value is provided, so it is not encoded as a numeric observation.
